paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God means what He says, and He says it plainly. He tells the land of Israel, "The end has come upon the four corners of the land," and He says He will judge them "according to your ways" (Ezekiel 7:2-3). Twice He adds that He will not look on them with pity or spare them, and both times the point is the same: "Then you will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 7:4, 9). I think God wants no one guessing about who He is.

Now look at what the people leaned on. Silver and gold were supposed to be safety, and God says they "cannot save them in the day of the wrath of the LORD," because wealth "became the stumbling block that brought their iniquity" (Ezekiel 7:19). Even their beautiful ornaments got turned into idols (Ezekiel 7:20). Friend, anything we trust more than God will let us down, and it does it at the worst possible moment. Nobody on that day gets to say, "I thought my savings account had my back."

So what do you do with a hard chapter like this one? You take God at His word while there's still time to listen. This one is heavy, and I think it's meant to be. It says the day is real, God's word is not taken back, and the safest thing we can hold is Him. Keep your hands steady, baker, and keep your trust where it belongs.
